climate_pressure: Rising temperature, increasing hot-day exposure and potentially worsening drought/reduced groundwater recharge.
documented_impact: Greater water stress, heat exposure and potential agricultural pressure.
fcv_mediator: Water-access arrangements, infrastructure condition, fiscal constraints, movement restrictions, markets and institutional capacity.
possible_consequence: Could deepen food, livelihood or service insecurity where households and institutions cannot substitute water, imports, income or services; violence is not demonstrated as an outcome.
geographies: with different exposure and institutional contexts
uncertainty: Contemporary climate-to-FCV causal outcomes have not been quantified.
resilience_factors: humanitarian WASH support and functioning institutional networks where maintained
compact_statement: Heat and drought may increase water/food stress, but FCV consequences depend on access, infrastructure, institutions and markets rather than following automatically from climate.

climate_pressure: More volatile rainfall and potentially more intense extreme events.
documented_impact: Significant modelled flood exposure in parts of the West Bank and flood/drainage risk in urban areas.
fcv_mediator: Damaged or insufficient drainage/WASH infrastructure, municipal capacity, movement/access constraints and fiscal resources.
possible_consequence: Flood events could cause greater service interruption, health risk or livelihood loss where repair and emergency access are constrained.
geographies: especially northwest/eastern and urban locations identified by the CCDR
Gaza requires a new post-destruction flood-exposure assessment
alternative_explanations: conflict damage and settlement patterns can independently determine flood losses
uncertainty: Gaza’s post-2023 asset/exposure geography invalidates many pre-conflict assumptions.
resilience_factors: resilient reconstruction and unrestricted emergency/service access
compact_statement: Flood hazard may become more damaging when infrastructure and delivery capacity are impaired, but current conflict damage should not itself be classified as climate impact.

climate_pressure: Sea-level rise, saltwater intrusion, warming and scenario-dependent rainfall/recharge decline.
documented_impact: Projected worsening pressure on Gaza groundwater quality and water scarcity.
fcv_mediator: Aquifer over-extraction, desalination/energy dependence, conflict-damaged WASH and electricity systems, restrictions on materials/fuel and financing.
possible_consequence: Climate pressure could increase the cost and difficulty of restoring safe water services and deepen reliance on external or energy-intensive supply.
affected_groups: children and communities dependent on damaged water networks
alternative_explanations: infrastructure destruction and power shortage can independently produce water-quality problems
uncertainty: No post-2023 study located isolates the incremental climate contribution to present Gaza water insecurity.
resilience_factors: aquifer management and diversified water supply
compact_statement: Gaza’s water vulnerability is a compound system problem; climate can add pressure, but current scarcity and contamination cannot be attributed to climate alone.

climate_pressure: Future heat, drought, flood and coastal hazards.
documented_impact: Current conflict has destroyed or damaged large shares of energy, WASH, housing and other service assets.
fcv_mediator: Direct infrastructure destruction, displacement, access/material restrictions, financing constraints and institutional disruption.
possible_consequence: These conditions likely reduce the capacity to prepare for, absorb and recover from future climate shocks compared with the pre-2023 policy baseline.
affected_groups: service workers and people with health vulnerabilities
alternative_explanations: infrastructure deficits and institutional constraints limited adaptation
uncertainty: The magnitude of lost climate-adaptation capacity has not been independently quantified.
compact_statement: The best-supported current Climate-FCV direction in Gaza is conflict reducing the systems needed to cope with future climate hazards.

climate_pressure: Increasing heat and potential drought/water stress.
documented_impact: OCHA reports current damage/removal of water infrastructure and increased emergency water-trucking dependence in specific Area C communities.
fcv_mediator: Demolitions, settler attacks, movement/access restrictions and land/grazing access.
possible_consequence: In affected herding communities, future drought could become harder to absorb because water storage, livestock watering and mobility options are already constrained.
geographies: Masafer Yatta and other documented communities
uncertainty: Current OCHA/UNICEF incidents do not themselves involve a measured drought shock, so the compound pathway remains prospective.
compact_statement: Damage and access restrictions can lower drought-coping capacity for specific West Bank herding communities even where climate was not the cause of the original water disruption.

climate_pressure: Multiple projected heat, drought, flood and water risks.
documented_impact: Climate investment requires substantial finance and institutional coordination.
fcv_mediator: PA fiscal crisis, revenue uncertainty, staffing constraints and pressure to prioritize immediate service and recovery needs.
possible_consequence: Climate-risk screening, infrastructure investment and NDC/NAP implementation may be delayed, reduced or re-prioritized.
geographies: implications for wider Palestinian climate planning
alternative_explanations: donor priorities and incomplete project preparation may also delay climate action
uncertainty: No current climate-budget expenditure tracing was located.
resilience_factors: protected maintenance budgets and institutional coordination
compact_statement: Severe fiscal stress plausibly crowds out long-term climate investment, but the size of that effect is not yet quantified.

climate_pressure: Applicable to future water, drought and flood shocks, though original evaluated shock was conflict-related.
documented_impact: After 2014 damage, project M&E and rapid assessment supported redesign, additional finance and WASH rehabilitation.
fcv_mediator: Ability of service institutions and donors to retain data, staff, financing and implementation flexibility during crisis.
possible_consequence: Comparable institutional capabilities could support future compound-shock recovery if they remain functional.
alternative_explanations: reconstruction access and external technical support contributed materially
uncertainty: The institutional baseline and destruction after 2023 are fundamentally different; persistence of this capability is unverified.
compact_statement: Historical evaluation shows that institutional learning and flexible finance can accelerate WASH recovery, but transferability to current Gaza is unproven.

climate_pressure: No climate shock is identified as the present primary driver; pathway concerns future compound food/livelihood stress.
documented_impact: IPC reports large-scale assistance improved food-security conditions after the October 2025 ceasefire, while severe food insecurity persists and is projected to worsen.
fcv_mediator: Humanitarian access, crossing conditions, markets, supply chains and funding.
possible_consequence: Reliable assistance could buffer households against additional climate-related livelihood shocks, while access disruptions could remove that buffer.
alternative_explanations: prices and household income also affect food security
uncertainty: IPC attribution is evidence synthesis, not experimental evaluation; climate-buffering effectiveness was not evaluated.
resilience_factors: diversified livelihoods and restored domestic food systems
compact_statement: Humanitarian assistance currently supplies critical coping capacity, but its role in climate resilience remains inferred rather than evaluated.
